full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this civil appeal, in short, are that plaintiff-respondent No.1 took loan of Taka 95,00,000 from the defendant-appellant, Janata Bank observing all the formalities. Interest of the said loan was 12½% per annum. There was stipulation in the sanction letter that the same would be re-payable with interest within 12 years and that the monthly instalment was fixed at Taka 1,26,425. In pursuance of the application filed by plaintiff-respondent No.1 on 26-8-1995, the instalment was rescheduled at Taka 1,40,000 per month. Plaintiff-respondent No.1 again filed an application on 30-12-2001 for rescheduling the said loan and accordingly, the instalment was fixed at Taka 2,62,000 per month and it was further stipulated that the total amount was to be repaid within 14-11-2012. On 30-12-2003, plaintiff-respondent No.1 again filed an application for rescheduling the loan amount which was allowed. Accordingly, the instalment was rescheduled at Taka 3,08,000 per month. Plaintiff-respondent No.1 filed an application for exemption of interest which was rejected on 20-10-2011 and the bank directed him to repay the overdue amount of Taka 1,13,96,000 within 15-11-2011. Thereafter, the bank issued impugned `final notice' on 21-11-2011 requesting plaintiff-respondent No.1 to pay the said amount of Taka 1,13,96,000 by 30-11-2011. Feeling aggrieved by the said notice, plaintiff-respondent No.1 filed the title suit for declaration. 

 3. The appellant-bank contested the suit stating, inter alia, that a sum of Taka 95,00,000 was sanctioned in favour of plaintiff-respondent No.1 on the basis of the prayer made by him [plaintiff-respondent No.1). Plaintiff-respondent No.1 was defaulted to repay the said amount and lastly on 30-12-2003, monthly instalment was fixed to the tune of Taka 3,08,000 per month and be payable by 14-11-2012. But plaintiff-respondent No.1 failed to pay the instalment regularly. The defaulted amount stood Taka 1,13,96,000 and plaintiff-respondent No.1 was directed to pay the said amount within 30-11-2011 by the final notification. The suit was not maintainable and the same should be dismissed. 

 4. The learned Judge of the trial Court dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff-respondent preferred First Appeal No. 265 of 2013 before the High Court Division. The learned Judges of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and decree allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 6. Mr Khaled Ahmed, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant-bank, submits that the suit was not at all maintainable. Admittedly, plaintiff-respondent No.1 took loan of Taka 95,00,000 and he failed to repay the instalments regularly and consequently, the defaulted amount stood Taka 1,13,96,000 and thus, plaintiff-respondent No.1 was requested to deposit the said amount by the impugned notice dated 21-11-2011 and that there was no illegality in the final notice. He further submits that plaintiff-respondent No.1 challenged the notice dated 21-11-2011 having been served upon him by the appellant-bank claiming Taka 1,13,96,000 which was a request to pay the defaulted loan money under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The original loan was sanctioned at Taka 95,00,000 on 7-9-1994 in favour of plaintiff-respondent No.1 and the loan was rescheduled subsequently on several times, therefore, on the notice dated 21-11-2011 the defaulted loan money stood at Taka 1,13,96,000 but the High Court Division has given a wrong finding that the appellant-bank cannot claim any amount more than 300% of the original loan money without considering that the case was not originated from the judgment of an Artha Rin Adalat. He further submits that the subject matter of the case is under the jurisdiction of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, whereas, the plaintiff-respondent filed the suit before a Joint District Judge who has no jurisdiction to hear the subject matter of the Artha Rin Adalat case. It is further submitted that the loan of the borrower would be calculated after the reschedule of the loan but not from the date of original sanction rather from the date of rescheduling. This aspect of the matter was not at all considered by the High Court Division. It is also submitted that based on the application dated 16-1-2003 of plaintiff respondent No.1, the day of last reschedule, was fixed on 30-12-2003 and the rescheduled loan was fixed at an amount of Taka 1,76,36,000 as per section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, the highest loan can be stood at the amount of Taka 5,23,08,000, whereas, the High Court Division calculated the loan at Taka 95,00,000 based on the date of (1st) sanction letter. 

 7. Per contra, Mr M. Sayed Ahmed, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent No.1, contends that since the plaintiff-respondent repaid more than 300% of the principal amount, the appellant-bank was not entitled to issue the final notice. Referring to section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, he further contends that the final notice as issued, is not legal as per section 12 of the said Ain, 2003 and it was served for selling the mortgaged property without giving any chance to the borrower to raise any objection and, as such, the suit filed by the plaintiff-respondent, has cause of action. Therefore, the High Court Division rightly allowed the appeal and decreed the suit. 

 9. The claim of the plaintiff-respondent is that on his application, defendant No.2-Janata Bank Ltd, Topkhana Road Corporate Branch, by letter No. TOP/AGRIM/708/98 dated 7-9-1994 sanctioned a loan of Taka 95,00,000 [ordinary house building loan (commercial)] imposing 12.50% compound interest refund-able within 12 years. Defendant No.2 by letter bearing Memo No.TOP/AGRIM/SA:/GRIH:/NI:/RIN:/ MOYAZZEM/PUNTAFSIL/HASA-NAT-2002 dated 3-1-2002 allegedly stated to have received an application for liquidation of loan period from 14-11-2006 to 14-11-2012 and the monthly instalment of Taka 2,62,000 in place of 1,40,000. The plaintiff-respondent having availed the loan facility utilized the loan money in construction, but he failed to repay the loan money in due time. So, the plaintiff-respondent wrote to defendant No.2 on 24-7-2005 for considering the calculation of compound interest into a simple interest by EXIT Procedure. In the meantime, the plaintiff-respondent liquidated the loan including interest of Taka 1,02,00,000 only. The plaintiff-respondent wrote several letters to defendant Nos.1 and 2 on 5-1-2006, 6-3-2006, 3-4-2007, 14-1-2008, 21-4-2008 and 15-9-2008 requesting them to allow benefit of repayment of loan on EXIT Procedure as because EXIT procedure benefit has already been given to pro-forma defendant No.3, but they did not pay heed to that effect. It is further alleged that the plaintiff-respondent by letter dated 4-7-2011 requested the Chairman, Janata Bank Ltd to settle the loan matter of 95,00,000 sanctioned in his favour. The plaintiff-respondent sought protection of law in the light of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Though the plaintiff-respondent requested for remission of loan through EXIT procedure, defendant No.2 by letter No.SUTRA:AGM/ SA:GRE:NI:RIN/ SUD MOUKUF/2011/3 dated 20-7-2011 illegally and in violation of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 converted the name into a loan of compound interest in place of simple interest and wrote to the plaintiff-respondent by letter Memo No. SUTRA-MH/SA: GRE:NI: RIN/2011/7 dated 21-11-2011 for realization of Taka 1,13,96,000. 

 10. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid letter, plaintiff-respondent No.1 prayed for a decree upon Memo No. SUTRA-MH/SA:GRE:NI:RIN/ 2011/7 dated 21-11-2011 claiming Taka 1,13,96,000, issued under the signature of defendant No.2 by the instruction of defendant No.1 to be declared illegal, void, malafide and not binding upon plaintiff-respondent No. 1 . He also prayed for permanent injunction restraining defendant Nos.1 and 2 from selling mortgaged property under section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Amending the plaint, plaintiff-respondent No.1 prayed for (c) A Decree in his favour that be pleased to restrain the defendant Nos.1 and 2 from giving effect of the subsequdnt legal notice dated 11-3-2013 threatening the plaintiff respondent to initiate the sale process of mortgaged property under section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, is not binding upon him. 

 11. On the other hand, the appellant-bank claims that plaintiff-respondent No.1, after taking loan, paid some instalments amounting to Taka 2,68,07,624, in total, upto 5-9-2008. Thereafter, plaintiff-respondent No.1 failed to repay the remaining instalment. It stands at Taka 1,13,96,000 upto 29-12-2011. The plaintiff-respondent was requested to deposit the aforesaid money by a notice dated 21-11-2011 and there was no illegality in. the impugned notice. The notice was nothing but a request to pay the defaulted loan money. Against the said notice, the plaintiff-respondent filed a suit in the Court of Joint District Judge seeking relief under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which is a serious error of law. It is further revealed that on the notice dated 21-11-2011 defaulted loan money stood at Taka 1,13,96,000 and the High Court Division gave wrong finding that the appellant-bank cannot claim any amount more than 300% of the original loan money without considering that the case was not originated from the judgment of an Artha Rin Adalat. It is obvious that the subject matter of the case is under the jurisdiction of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The loan of the borrower would be calculated from the date of rescheduling. This aspect of the matter was not at all considered by the High Court Division. 

 12. On perusal of the documents on record, it reveals that admittedly the plaintiff-respondent could not pay the loan money, taken on 6-9-1994, within 12 years. Rather, the plaintiff-respondent applied for rescheduling the instalment on several times by filing applications. The defendant-appellant granted those applications. Since the loan was rescheduled, the amount of loan money would not limit in 95,00,000. The plaintiff-respondent would have to pay the loan money with the rescheduled rate. 

 15. The plaintiff-respondent failed to make payment to the appellant-bank as per terms and conditions made between them but the appellant-bank on several occasions rescheduled the defaulted loan money on the prayer of the plaintiff-respondent. It appears from the record that the appellant-bank had showed utmost sympathy to the plaintiff-respondent so that he could adjust the loan money borrowed by him along with interest as per bank rules. 

 16. It is to be borne in mind that if the borrower fails to pay the borrowed money within the time stipulated, then, naturally the interest of loan money will remain increased. Because of negligence of the plaintiff-respondent, this incidence occurred in the present case. As a result, a big amount of money has been figured against the loan money. However, this matter is absolutely related to the transactions made in the defendant-bank with the plaintiff-respondent borrower. If there has been any illegality committed in the assessment of the rate of interest by the appellant-bank, that could have been adjudicated by filing suit in the Artha Rin Adalat, but not in the civil Court. 

 17. The plaintiff-respondent challenged the final notice dated 21-11-2011 issued by the appellant-bank which is reproduced below for better understanding: 

 18. On plain reading of the said notice, it has been disclosed that it was a mere request to the borrower. The appellant-bank only reminded the plaintiff-respondent for adjustment of the loan money borrowed by him. Though it was a final notice served upon the plaintiff-respondent, it did not create any cause of action so that the plaintiff-respondent could have been aggrieved to file a suit for declaration upon the said final notice to be illegal, void, malafide and not binding upon him. Apart from this, it is also seen from the record that the appellant-bank also issued a legal notice dated 11-3-2013 through its lawyer after around two years of the final notice dated 21-11-2011 was issued, which indicates that the bank used to make correspondence with the plaintiff-respondent to settle and adjust the borrowed money prior to emerging any cause of action to be preferred in the Artha Rin Adalat as per Artha Rin Ain. Since the matter was premature one, the suit brought by the plaintiff-respondent before the civil court was not maintainable in the eye of law.
